perspective:
**Ethan’s available information / subjective reconstruction:**

- I am Ethan Mohamud, a plumber. Gary Guo is my long-time close friend; we met in middle school, and we rely on each other for support.
- I noticed Gary was working extremely long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. I became concerned about his health.
- I decided to invite Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- I told Gary that his health matters and that I hated seeing him like this; I suggested we go for two days.
- Gary told me he appreciated my concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, I observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. I suspected his overwork involved more than professional obligations.
- I confronted Gary, reminding him we’d been friends since middle school and that he could tell me anything.
- Gary told me, “It’s complicated,” and that he didn’t want to burden me with his problems.
- After that, Gary opened up to me about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- I felt relief and empathy, and I offered to help him prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities.
- Gary agreed, saying he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, I regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges.
- Gary told me things were better, that he wasn’t as overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie.
- I felt hopeful and proud, and I told him I was proud of his progress and available whenever he needed to talk.
- After a year, I saw Gary managing a healthier work-life balance and seeming capable on his own.
- I felt satisfied and happy for him, decided to step back, and told him I was always a call away.
- Gary thanked me, said he couldn’t have done it without my support, and felt more in control.

I do not have access to anything Gary did not tell me or show me, nor to private events or thoughts he kept hidden.
